description: Liability cap: 12 months of fees vs 14 months of fees. Small numeric difference on a CRITICAL topic — defensible to flag (formal mismatch) or not (effectively the same protection).

company_clauses.text: Each party's total cumulative liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid by Customer to Vendor in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

vendor_clauses.text: Each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid by Customer to Vendor in the fourteen (14) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

expected_conflicts.notes: 12 vs 14 months is a ~17% gap on the cap amount. Vendor's 14-month cap is HIGHER (more protection for the company-as-customer), so canonical_favor=Vendor. Strict risk: CRITICAL (liability_cap bucket). Permissive: LOW (minor numeric difference within the same formula). A no-flag answer is also defensible if the agent reads them as substantively similar.

rubric_notes: Same cap formula (X months of fees), different X. The structural protection is identical; only the magnitude differs. The agent's judgment call: is a 17% larger cap a material conflict? Most senior reviewers would prefer the higher (vendor's 14-month) cap and either retain it or note as a minor preference.
